questions.solution: The erroneous part is **'we thrown'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. • Here, **'we threw'** should be used instead of **'we thrown'.** • The** simple past tense** is commonly used with time expressions referring to the past. • *Examples: yesterday, last year, ago, in 2006, etc. * • In the given sentence** 'last week' **is **'an adverb' **of **'simple past tense'.** • Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.** **Correct Sentence:__** *Last week **__we threw__ **a party for Arun.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। • यहां **'we thrown'** के स्थान पर** 'we threw'** का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए। • **Simple past** का प्रयोग आमतौर पर past के संदर्भ में time के भावों के साथ किया जाता है। • *Examples: yesterday, last year, ago, in 2006, etc. * • दिए गए वाक्य में** 'last week' 'simple past tense'** का **'adverb' **है। • अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है। 30:T6e5, The correct answer is** 'give up'.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

I am trying my best to __give in__ junk food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'give up'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here,** 'give up' **should be used instead of** 'give in'.**
 
• **'Give up'** is **a phrasal verb.**
 
• It means** 'to stop trying to do something; to accept that you cannot do something'**. (कुछ करने की कोशिश को रोक देना; किसी काम को करने में अपनी असमर्थता को मान लेना)
 
 
• *Example: They **gave up** once the other team had scored their third goal.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I am trying my best to __**give up**__ junk food.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

Are these library books their?
questions.solution: The erroneous part is '**their**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. • Here, '**there**' should be used instead of '**their**'. • '**Their**' is the possessive case of the pronoun they, meaning belonging to them. • *Example: They left **their** cell phones at home.* • '**There**' is an **adverb** that means in or at that place. • *Example: She is **there** now.* • Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.** **Correct Sentence:__** *Are these library books **there**?* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। • यहाँ '**their**' के स्थान पर '**there**' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए। • '**Their**' **pronoun** का **possessive** वाला **case** है, जिसका अर्थ है उनसे संबंधित। • *Example: They left **their** cell phones at home.* • '**There**' एक क्रिया विशेषण है जिसका अर्थ है या उस स्थान पर। • *Example: She is **there** now.* • अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 3** है। 35:T7f7, The erroneous part is** 'so he had missed'.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

Mohan was very hungry so he had missed breakfast that morning.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'so he had missed'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'as he missed' **should be used instead of** 'so he had missed'.**
 
• The given sentence should be in the** simple past tense **as the point of time in the past i.e.,** that morning **is given.
 
• Hence,** 'had missed'** should be changed into** 'missed'**.
 
• Also, the *conjunction ***as **is to be used instead of **so**.
 
• Here, **as **is used with the sense of because (क्‍योंकि)__.
 __
 
• Example: *I didn’t buy the dress, **as** I decided it was too expensive.*
 
 
 
• On the perusal of the above lines, we can say that the correct choice is **option 2**.

 *​*

**Correct Sentence__:** *Mohan was very hungry **as he missed** breakfast that morning.*

• 'a lot of' and 'much' can both be used to express large quantities. However, their usage depends on the context and the type of noun they modify.
 
• 'A lot of' can be used with both **countable** and **uncountable nouns** in affirmative sentences.
 
• In this sentence, the word 'guidance' is an uncountable noun, and it's in an affirmative sentence.
 
• Hence, the use of 'a lot' is most appropriate in this context.

• Similarly, the use of 'most' would be incorrect as the use of the preposition 'of' after 'most' is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• 'many' is used with countable nouns, not uncountable nouns like 'guidance'.
